subject.title: fix(cron): bound cron quarantine sidecar file reads

question: Should cron overflow recovery silently retain only five sidecar archives, or should archive lifecycle remain non-destructive and operator/Doctor-owned?
rationale: The cap and rotation are bounded technical repairs, but choosing when historic recovery records may be deleted determines user-visible recoverability and operational data retention.

options.title: Doctor-owned archive lifecycle
options.body: Keep bounded reads and rotation, but move inspection and cleanup of recovery archives to an explicit Doctor/operator flow rather than deleting them during cron writes.

options.title: Approve five-file retention
options.body: Accept automatic pruning as a deliberate recovery-data retention policy and document that the oldest archive is deleted after the fifth retained file.

options.title: Limit this PR to caps
options.body: Land only the bounded read/write behavior and defer archive rotation plus retention to a separately sponsored recovery-design change.

recommendation.title: Doctor-owned archive lifecycle
recommendation.body: Keep bounded reads and rotation, but move inspection and cleanup of recovery archives to an explicit Doctor/operator flow rather than deleting them during cron writes.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR explicitly asks steipete to decide the archive-retention policy.
